battery_replacement_cost_note: One replacement occurs in ownership year 10. Replacement retains each TIGER vehicle's modeled battery capacity but uses the pack-level Battery Cost (2022$/kWh) attached to the exact selected 2024 Transportation ATB vehicle configuration. Study Conservative, Reference, and Optimistic map to raw ATB Conservative, Mid, and Advanced battery trajectories, respectively. Values are interpolated between ATB milestones and converted from 2022 to 2023 USD.
scooter_battery_swapping_cost_note: 2025 Taiwan battery-swapping cost range is preserved. Conservative holds the observed fee constant. Reference and Optimistic change only the network battery-capital component: C_swap(t)=C_swap(2025)+n_bat*B[c_NMC(t)-c_NMC(2025)]/L_bat, with n_bat=2.2 effective batteries per scooter, B=1.3 kWh, and L_bat=64,000 km (10 years x 6,400 km/yr). The effective inventory is based on Gogoro network-level battery counts relative to supported scooters/riders. The NMC trajectory uses 137 USD/kWh (2023), 100 (2030), and 80 (2050), linearly interpolated.

depot_charging.cost_method_note: 150-kW depot charger hardware and installation bounds follow Moreno-Sader et al. (2025), with the Reference case equal to their midpoint. The 12-h charging window and 20/40/60% utilization values are explicit infrastructure scenarios in this study, not values reported by Moreno-Sader.
depot_charging.initial_stock_method: 2024 requirements are estimated separately from observed electric light-truck, bus, and heavy-truck registrations using 2025 energy-use assumptions.
depot_charging.taipower_tariff_note: For 150-kW bus/heavy-truck depot charging, Taipower high-voltage EV tariff rates are modeled as 95% of the low-voltage EV tariff. Annualized low-voltage off-peak energy and contract-capacity rates are 2.95 NT$/kWh and 38.8 NT$/kW-month before the 5% high-voltage reduction. The fixed 262.5 NT$/month customer charge is site-level and is excluded from per-charger delivered cost because chargers per site are not specified.
depot_charging.light_truck_cost_note: Light-truck depot charging uses a 50-kW charger. Installed cost is proxied by the 50-kW DCFC equipment + installation cost reported by Borlaug et al. (2020), converted at the model exchange rate.

public_charging.residential_charging_note: Passenger-car residential charging energy share. Conservative=30%, Reference=40%, and Optimistic=50% are scenario assumptions chosen to reflect constrained residential charging access in Taiwan, particularly in multi-unit housing. Light trucks are modeled separately with 50-kW depot charging.
public_charging.charging_mix_note: Passenger-car non-residential charging energy is split 75% workplace/public L2 and 25% DCFC. This approximates Borlaug et al. (2020), whose BEV baseline uses 14% workplace/public L2 and 5% DCFC of total charging energy (73.7%/26.3% within non-residential charging).
public_charging.note: Observed 2024 passenger-car public charger cohorts are initialized using the reported Taiwan stock of 7,379 slow and 2,391 fast ports. From 2025 onward, requirements are sized from passenger-car fleet electricity demand, scenario-specific residential charging shares, a 75/25 L2/DCFC energy split, charger power, and scenario-specific utilization. Light trucks are modeled separately with 50-kW depot charging. Vehicle technology and charging assumptions are evaluated independently in a 3x3 factorial design.
public_charging.cost_note: Installed costs are taken directly from Borlaug et al. (2020): public/workplace L2 = 3,500 USD equipment + 2,500 USD installation = 6,000 USD/port; 50-kW DCFC = 38,000 USD equipment + 20,000 USD installation = 58,000 USD/port. Values are converted at the model exchange rate.
public_charging.observed_stock_note: Taiwan MOTC reported 9,770 public charging ports in December 2024: 7,379 slow and 2,391 fast ports. These observed counts initialize the two public charger cohorts separately.
public_charging.utilization_note: Reference L2 utilization (18%) corresponds to about 30 kWh/day at a 7-kW port, matching Borlaug et al. (2020). Other L2 and all DCFC utilization values are explicit future planning scenarios; Borlaug et al. (2023) documents low and highly variable observed public utilization.

technology_trajectory_note: Manuscript 'ATB Baseline' is an alias for the raw 'Conservative' vehicle trajectory in 2024_atb_transportation_data_v1/output/vehicles.csv. It is used by the manuscript Reference scenario.
phev_efficiency_trajectory_note: PHEV operating efficiency is modeled separately by mode using the selected 2024 Transportation ATB Midsize Gasoline Power Split PHEV (30-mile electric range). Study Conservative / Reference / Optimistic use raw ATB Constant / Mid / Advanced CS/CD trajectories, respectively. Charge-sustaining fuel-mode energy use scales with CS_2025/CS_t and charge-depleting electric-mode energy use scales with CD_t/CD_2025. Each trajectory is normalized to its own 2025 value; the Taiwan-specific 2025 mode-energy anchors are retained.
